answer: In a market for ferrous scrap, one escrowed stake unit buys one live bidding slot until its dispute window closes. Each beacon pulse starts a fresh auction. The ledger binds each slot to one signed bid receipt and rejects a second use. Splitting the same stake across a hundred keys buys no more slots. To gain a hundred slots, a farm must tie up a hundred stake units and pay a nonrefundable fee on each. This prices influence without pretending to know who owns every key.
